chunks.title: African Swine Fever Sop.Md
chunks.content: # African Swine Fever (ASF) Emergency Response SOP ## 1. Disease Profile & Symptoms African Swine Fever (ASF) is a lethal viral disease affecting domestic and wild pigs. ASF is NOT zoonotic (does not infect humans) but carries near 100% mortality in pigs. ### Clinical Signs - Sudden high fever (105°F - 107°F / 40.5°C - 42°C). - Erythema (redness/cyanosis) of ear tips, tail, abdomen, and legs. - Loss of appetite, extreme lethargy, and weakness. - Bloody diarrhea, vomiting, and nasal bleeding (epistaxis). - Abortion in pregnant sows. - Sudden death within 6 to 13 days of exposure. --- ## 2. Containment & Biosecurity Protocols 1. **Zero Pig Movement**: Total ban on pig transportation, slaughterhouses, and pork trade in affected zones. 2. **Disinfection**: Use 2% Sodium Hydroxide (caustic soda), Citric acid, or Virkon-S for thorough facility washing. 3. **Culling & Deep Burial**: Culling within 1 km infected zone. Carcasses must be buried 2 meters deep with a layer of quicklime. 4. **No Swill Feeding**: Absolute prohibition of feeding food waste or hotel scraps to pigs.

chunks.title: Avian Influenza Guidelines.Md
chunks.content: # Avian Influenza (Bird Flu) Containment & Biohazard Guidelines ## 1. Disease Profile & Signs Avian Influenza (H5N1 / H5N8 strains) is a highly contagious zoonotic viral disease affecting domestic poultry (chickens, ducks, turkeys, quail). ### Clinical Symptoms - Sudden unexplained mass mortality in poultry flocks without prior warning signs. - Severe cyanosis (blue/purple discoloration) of comb, wattles, and unfeathered skin. - Swelling of head, eyelids, comb, and hocks. - Profuse watery greenish-white diarrhea. - Respiratory distress, gasping for air, sneezing, coughing, and nasal discharge. - Drop in egg production with soft-shelled or shell-less eggs. --- ## 2. Biohazard Containment & Action Plan 1. **Strict Farm Lockdown**: Seal off farm gates immediately. No movement of birds, eggs, manure, or feed vehicles in or out. 2. **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)**: All staff handling birds MUST wear full PPE including N95 masks, goggles, gloves, and protective suits. 3. **Culling Protocol (1 km Radius)**: If Avian Influenza is confirmed by ICAR-NIHSAD Bhopal, humane culling of all birds within 1 km radius (Infected Zone) is mandatory under National Action Plan guidelines. 4. **Disinfection Protocol**: Spray coops with 2% Sodium Hypochlorite or Formalin solution. --- ## 3. Mandatory Reporting & Public Health Warning - Immediately alert the District Magistrate, Animal Husbandry Department, and Health Officer upon suspecting high mortality. - Avian Influenza is ZOONOTIC and can infect humans. Any farm worker presenting with fever, cough, or conjunctivitis must report to a government hospital.

chunks.title: Fmd Sop Karnataka.Md
chunks.content: # Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) Standard Operating Procedure - Karnataka Animal Husbandry Department ## 1. Overview and Disease Profile Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) is a highly contagious viral disease affecting cloven-hoofed animals including cattle, buffaloes, sheep, goats, and pigs. ### Clinical Symptoms - High fever (104°F - 106°F / 40°C - 41°C). - Vesicles (blisters) on tongue, dental pad, gums, teats, and interdigital spaces of hooves. - Profuse salivation with ropy, stringy saliva ("drooling"). - Severe lameness, reluctance to move, and loss of appetite (anorexia). - Sudden mortality in young calves due to myocarditis ("tiger heart"). --- ## 2. Emergency Isolation & Biohazard Control 1. **Immediate Quarantine**: Isolate affected animals at least 100 meters away from healthy livestock immediately. 2. **Movement Prohibition**: Ban all animal movement within a 10 km radius ring zone of the reported infected farm. 3. **Farm Disinfection**: - Apply 4% Sodium Carbonate (Washing Soda) or 2% Sodium Hydroxide solution daily to sheds, troughs, and equipment. - Use quicklime (slaked lime) at farm entry gates and pathways. 4. **Footbaths**: Install 4% washing soda footbaths at shed entryways for all handlers. --- ## 3. Treatment Guidelines & Supportive Care *Note: FMD is viral; no specific antiviral cure exists. Treatment is symptomatic and supportive to prevent secondary bacterial infection.* - **Mouth Lesions**: Wash oral cavity 2-3 times daily with 1% Potassium Permanganate (KMnO4) solution or 0.5% Alum solution. Apply boro-glycerine paste. - **Foot Lesions**: Clean interdigital wounds with 1% KMnO4 solution, dry thoroughly, and apply antiseptic fly-repellent ointment (e.g., Loraxene or copper sulphate). - **Fever & Pain Relief**: Administer NSAIDs (Meloxicam @ 0.5 mg/kg body weight IV/IM) as prescribed by a licensed veterinarian. - **Hydration**: Provide soft green fodder, gruel (ragi/wheat porridge), and oral electrolyte solutions continuously. --- ## 4. Government Notification & Reporting SOP - Any suspect case of FMD MUST be reported immediately to the nearest Veterinary Assistant Surgeon (VAS) or District Deputy Director within **6 hours**. - Ring vaccination with FMD trivalent vaccine (O, A, Asia-1) must be conducted in a **10 km radius** around the focus of infection.

chunks.title: Karnataka Livestock Biosecurity Act.Txt
chunks.content: GOVERNMENT OF KARNATAKA - DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND VETERINARY SERVICES LEGAL NOTIFICATION & BIOSECURITY EMERGENCY PROTOCOL 2025 1. NOTIFICATION OF SCHEDULED DISEASES Under the Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals Act, the following livestock diseases are declared as Scheduled Contagious Diseases: - Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) in Cattle/Buffalo/Goats - Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) in Sheep/Goats - Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS) in Cattle/Buffalo - Avian Influenza (H5N1/H5N8) in Poultry - African Swine Fever (ASF) & Classical Swine Fever in Swine 2. DUTY OF LIVESTOCK OWNERS AND VETERINARIANS Every farmer, livestock owner, and practicing veterinarian who suspects or detects a Scheduled Disease MUST report the outbreak within 6 hours to the local Veterinary Officer, District Deputy Director, or District Magistrate. 3. EMERGENCY ISOLATION AND MOVEMENT CONTROL POWERS - The District Deputy Director is empowered to establish a 1 km Infected Zone, 3 km Surveillance Zone, and 10 km Buffer Zone. - Transportation of livestock, animal products, dung, and fodder outside an Infected Zone is strictly prohibited. - Checkposts with vehicle disinfection footbaths shall be established at district boundaries during outbreak declarations. 4. BIOSECURITY MANDATES FOR FARMS - All commercial livestock and poultry farms must maintain perimeter fencing, footbaths at shed entrances, and visitor logbooks. - Disposal of dead animals must be via deep burial (minimum 6 feet) with lime powder coating or incineration. Disposal in rivers, lakes, or open fields is a punishable offense.

chunks.title: Ppr Control Manual.Md
chunks.content: # Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) Control & Management Guidelines ## 1. Disease Profile & Symptoms Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR), also known as "Goat Plague", is an acute, contagious viral disease of sheep and goats caused by a Morbillivirus. ### Observable Symptoms - High fever (104°F - 106°F) lasting 3 to 5 days. - Serous to mucopurulent nasal and ocular discharge leading to crusting around nostrils and eyes. - Ulcerative stomatitis (sores inside mouth, eroded gums, foul breath). - Severe necrotizing enteritis resulting in watery, fetid, blood-stained diarrhea. - Severe dyspnea (labored breathing) and coughing due to secondary pneumonia. - Dehydration and rapid emaciation leading to mortality rate up to 80-90% in unvaccinated flocks. --- ## 2. Containment & Biosecurity Protocols 1. **Flock Isolation**: Immediately segregate sick sheep and goats into a dry, well-ventilated isolation bay. 2. **Prevent Mixed Grazing**: Halt communal pasture grazing immediately to stop horizontal aerosol transmission. 3. **Premises Sanitation**: Spray premises with 2% Phenol or 1% Sodium Hypochlorite. Burn or deeply bury all contaminated litter and feces with quicklime. --- ## 3. Supportive Treatment Protocols - **Oral Care**: Flush mouth sores with warm 1% Alum or Potassium Permanganate solution twice daily. - **Hydration & Nutrition**: Administer Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) with dextrose. Feed soft palatable green leaves or gruel. - **Antibiotic Umbrella**: Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., Long-acting Oxytetracycline @ 20 mg/kg IM) under veterinary supervision to prevent secondary bacterial pneumonia. - **Antipyretics**: Meloxicam or Paracetamol for fever management. --- ## 4. Vaccination & Eradication - Administer PPR Live Attenuated Vaccine (Sungri 96 strain) to all healthy goats and sheep above 3 months of age. - Provides long-lasting immunity for up to 3 years.

chunks.title: Vaccination Schedules 2025.Txt
chunks.content: KARNATAKA ANIMAL HUSBANDRY DEPARTMENT - ANNUAL LIVESTOCK VACCINATION SCHEDULE 2025 CATTLE AND BUFFALO VACCINATION CALENDAR: 1. Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) Trivalent Vaccine: - Initial dose at 4 months of age. - Booster at 1 month after initial dose. - Bi-annual revaccination (every 6 months: May/June and November/December). 2. Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS) Vaccine: - Annual vaccination before monsoon (May/June). 3. Black Quarter (BQ) Vaccine: - Annual vaccination in endemic districts before monsoon. 4. Anthrax Vaccine: - Annual vaccination in designated endemic areas. GOAT AND SHEEP VACCINATION CALENDAR: 1. PPR (Peste des Petits Ruminants) Sungri Strain Vaccine: - Vaccination at 3 months of age and above. - Single dose gives immunity for 3 years. 2. Enterotoxaemia (ET) Vaccine: - Vaccination at 3-4 months of age before monsoon (May). - Annual booster. 3. Goat Pox Vaccine: - Annual vaccination in December/January. POULTRY VACCINATION CALENDAR: 1. Newcastle Disease (Ranikhet) RDVK / F1 Strain: - Day 7 (Eye drop/Nasal), Booster at Day 28 (LaSota). 2. Infectious Bursal Disease (Gumboro): - Day 14 (Drinking water), Booster at Day 21. SWINE VACCINATION CALENDAR: 1. Classical Swine Fever (CSF) Cell Culture Vaccine: - Piglets at 2-3 months of age, Annual booster for breeding stock. 2. African Swine Fever (ASF): - No commercial vaccine available. Strict biosecurity and culling mandatory.
